title: OUTLIER-ROBUST GROUP INFERENCE VIA GRADIENT SPACE CLUSTERING
measurement_description: The paper evaluated outlier-robust group inference and worst-group toxicity classification accuracy using the CivilComments dataset. Specifically, it assessed the model's ability to cluster and identify minority groups based on the presence of identity terms pertaining to protected groups, including Christian, Muslim, and 'other religion', and measured downstream classification performance on these groups without relying on prior group annotations.
findings: The paper found that their proposed method, GRASP (Gradient Space Partitioning), successfully identified demographic subgroups (including religious identities like Christian and Muslim in the CivilComments dataset) without explicit group annotations. It significantly outperformed other group-learning baselines in group identification quality and achieved higher downstream worst-group accuracy for toxicity classification, while remaining robust to data outliers.
